provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Electoral bodies
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the functions of INEC
The students should be able to explain the electoral process
The students should be able to participate in an election simulation

Introduction:
We have learned about government structures in Nigeria. Today we will look at the Independent National Electoral Commission and how elections work in our country.

Content:
INEC is the body that organizes elections in Nigeria. Its main job is to ensure free and fair elections. INEC registers voters, sets polling dates, and announces results. For example, during the last general election, INEC used the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System to reduce fraud. The electoral process includes voter registration, campaigning, voting, and result announcement. In Nigeria, we use ballot papers and sometimes electronic voting machines.

Class activity:
Students will conduct a mock election for class prefect. They will register as voters, create party manifestos, vote using ballot papers, and count results under supervision.

Evaluation questions:
What does INEC stand for?
List two functions of INEC.
Why is free and fair election important?

Summary:
Electoral bodies like INEC play a crucial role in ensuring our democracy works properly through organizing credible elections.

topics.title: Political parties
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different political parties in Nigeria
The students should be able to explain the role of political parties in democracy
The students should be able to create a party manifesto

Introduction:
Last week we learned about electoral bodies. Today we will discuss political parties which present candidates for elections and shape our democracy.

Content:
Political parties are groups of people with similar ideas who seek to win elections and govern. In Nigeria, we have parties like APC, PDP, and Labour Party. Each party has a manifesto which is a list of promises to the people if they win. For example, a party might promise to build more schools or fix bad roads. Parties choose candidates through primaries and campaign across the country using posters, rallies, and jingles like the popular 'Sai Baba' slogan.

Class activity:
Students will form small political parties, create names and symbols, and prepare a three-point manifesto addressing issues in the school or local community.

Evaluation questions:
What is a political party?
Name two political parties in Nigeria.
What is a manifesto?
Why do political parties have different symbols?

Summary:
Political parties are essential for democracy as they provide choice to voters and represent different interests in society.

topics.title: Public service in democracy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define public service
The students should be able to explain accountability in public service
The students should be able to identify service standards

Introduction:
We have studied how we choose our leaders through elections. Today we will examine how public servants serve the people in a democratic system.

Content:
Public service refers to the work done by government officials to serve the people. These workers include teachers, doctors, civil servants, and police officers. Accountability means public servants must answer for their actions and use public money wisely. For example, a local government chairman must account for how he spends the monthly allocation from the federal government. Service standards are the expected levels of performance, like teachers coming to school on time or health centers having enough medicine.

Class activity:
Students will role-play scenarios where they complain about poor public service and practice making constructive suggestions for improvement.

Evaluation questions:
What is public service?
Why is accountability important in public service?
Give an example of service standard in your school.

Summary:
Public service in democracy requires accountability and high standards to ensure citizens get the services they deserve.

topics.title: Citizenship by registration
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain naturalisation
The students should be able to list requirements for citizenship
The students should be able to distinguish between birth and registered citizenship

Introduction:
We have learned about being citizens by birth in Nigeria. Today we will discuss how foreigners can become Nigerian citizens through registration.

Content:
Citizenship by registration is when a foreigner becomes a Nigerian citizen through a legal process called naturalisation. To be registered as a citizen, a person must be at least 21 years old, have lived in Nigeria for at least 15 years, be of good character, and intend to continue living in Nigeria. For example, a man from Ghana who has lived in Lagos for 20 years and contributed to the community can apply for Nigerian citizenship. The process involves application, interview, and swearing an oath of allegiance.

Class activity:
Students will interview someone who has gone through naturalisation process or create a role-play showing the steps to becoming a Nigerian citizen.

Evaluation questions:
What is naturalisation?
List three requirements for citizenship by registration.
How is citizenship by registration different from citizenship by birth?

Summary:
Citizenship by registration allows deserving foreigners to become Nigerian citizens after meeting specific requirements and going through proper legal procedures.

topics.title: Rights of the child
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the Child Rights Act
The students should be able to identify children's rights
The students should be able to explain how rights come with responsibilities

Introduction:
As young Nigerians, it is important to know your rights. Today we will learn about the rights of children protected by Nigerian law.

Content:
The Child Rights Act was passed in 2003 to protect children's rights in Nigeria. This law says all children have rights to education, health care, protection from abuse, and freedom of expression. For example, children have the right to go to school instead of being forced to work. They also have the right to be protected from harmful traditional practices like early marriage. Rights come with responsibilities - children must respect others, obey their parents and teachers, and take care of their property.

Class activity:
Students will create a children's rights charter for the classroom, listing rights and responsibilities for everyone to follow.

Evaluation questions:
What is the Child Rights Act?
Name three rights of children in Nigeria.
How do children's rights differ from adults' rights?

Summary:
The Child Rights Act protects children and ensures they can develop in a safe and nurturing environment.

topics.title: Human trafficking law
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain human trafficking
The students should be able to identify legal protections against trafficking
The students should be able to list ways to report trafficking cases

Introduction:
We have learned about children's rights. Today we will discuss a serious crime called human trafficking and how Nigerian law protects victims.

Content:
Human trafficking is when people are tricked or forced into work or exploitation against their will. In Nigeria, the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Law punishes traffickers with up to 14 years in prison. Legal protections include safe shelters for victims, witness protection programs, and special courts for trafficking cases. People can report trafficking to the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) by calling their toll-free line or visiting their office. For example, a girl promised a job in Europe but forced into prostitution can report to NAPTIP for help.

Class activity:
Students will design posters warning about human trafficking and listing contact information for help.

Evaluation questions:
What is human trafficking?
Name one legal protection for victims of trafficking.
How can someone report a case of human trafficking in Nigeria?

Summary:
Human trafficking is a serious crime in Nigeria, and the government has established laws and agencies to protect victims and punish offenders.

topics.title: Law enforcement
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the role of police in society
The students should be able to identify rights during police encounters
The students should be able to demonstrate respect for law enforcement

Introduction:
Last week we discussed human trafficking laws. Today we will learn about law enforcement officers, particularly the police, and how we should interact with them.

Content:
The Nigeria Police Force is responsible for maintaining law and order in our country. Police officers have the power to arrest criminals, investigate crimes, and protect citizens. When dealing with police, you have rights - you must identify yourself when asked, but you cannot be forced to make a statement without a lawyer present. For example, if a policeman stops you on the road, you should be polite, show your ID if requested, but not accept any illegal demands. Citizens should respect police officers who perform their duties properly while reporting those who abuse their power.

Class activity:
Students will role-play proper interactions with police officers in different scenarios like traffic stops or community policing situations.

Evaluation questions:
What is the main role of the police?
Name two rights you have when dealing with police.
How should citizens react to police misconduct?

Summary:
Law enforcement officers play a vital role in society, and citizens should respect them while knowing their own rights during interactions.

topics.title: Drugs and the law
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify prohibited substances
The students should be able to explain penalties for drug offenses
The students should be able to practice saying no to drugs

Introduction:
We have learned about law enforcement. Today we will discuss drugs and the laws that control their use in Nigeria to protect our society.

Content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) is responsible for fighting drug abuse and trafficking in Nigeria. Some prohibited substances include cannabis (Indian hemp), cocaine, heroin, and tramadol. The law forbids possessing, selling, or using these drugs. Penalties for drug offenses can include fines, imprisonment of up to 25 years, or both. For example, a person caught with cannabis might be fined N100,000 and sentenced to 2 years in prison. Young people should learn to say no to drugs and report drug activities to authorities or teachers.

Class activity:
Students will create anti-drug jingles and posters to discourage drug use among teenagers.

Evaluation questions:
What does NDLEA stand for?
Name two prohibited drugs in Nigeria.
What is one penalty for drug offenses?
Why is it important to say no to drugs?

Summary:
Drug laws exist to protect citizens from the dangers of substance abuse, and everyone should understand and obey these laws.

topics.title: Community service
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define community service
The students should be able to identify ways to serve the community
The students should be able to plan a class community service project

Introduction:
As responsible citizens, we have duties to our community beyond just obeying laws. Today we will learn about community service and how we can contribute to our society.

Content:
Community service is voluntary work done to help improve the community without payment. It helps develop responsibility and compassion in young people. Examples of community service include cleaning the school compound, helping elderly neighbors, organizing blood donation drives, or tutoring younger students. For instance, students in Lagos might organize a cleanup of a local market or start a library for children in their neighborhood. Community service teaches valuable life skills and builds a better society for everyone.

Class activity:
The class will plan and execute a community service project such as planting trees around the school or organizing a reading session for primary school pupils.

Evaluation questions:
What is community service?
Give two examples of community service activities.
How does community service benefit society?

Summary:
Community service is an important way for citizens to contribute positively to their communities and develop responsible citizenship.

topics.title: Revision and BECE practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer past BECE questions
The students should be able to identify key concepts in civic education
The students should be able to improve exam techniques

Introduction:
This week we will revise the topics we have studied this term and practice answering questions similar to what you will see in your BECE examination.

Content:
We will review important concepts like electoral bodies, political parties, public service, citizenship, child rights, human trafficking laws, law enforcement, drug laws, and community service. Students will work in groups to summarize key points from each topic. We will practice answering past BECE questions by reading questions carefully, identifying what is being asked, planning answers before writing, and using examples from Nigeria to support points. For example, when answering about INEC, you should mention specific functions like voter registration and conducting elections.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to answer past BECE questions and then exchange papers to mark and give feedback to each other.

Evaluation questions:
What have you found most challenging in civic education this term?
Which topic do you need more practice on?
How can you improve your exam technique?

Summary:
Regular revision and practice with past questions are essential for success in the BECE examination.
